extracted.intended_audience: authors and peer reviewers preparing or evaluating manuscripts submitted to The American Naturalist (ecology/evolution researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: A journal-issued checklist of expectations and best practices for authors and reviewers to maximize transparency and quality across empirical, meta-analytic, and theoretical manuscripts submitted to The American Naturalist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for The American Naturalist
rubrics_metrics.description: The American Naturalist seeks papers that cause readers to consider new ideas, merge existing ideas in new ways, rethink familiar ideas, or provide particularly compelling evidence for established ideas; theory and data papers are welcome in equal measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure their manuscript offers substantive intellectual contribution (novel synthesis, reframing, or compelling evidence). Methods papers should enable new questions or address existing questions in particularly effective ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript gives sufficient coverage to relevant existing ideas and does not inflate its own novelty by omitting mention of relevant published studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may cite reviews and syntheses but should cite original sources for key new insights when possible. Avoid overstating novelty by omission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and clarity of writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should be thorough but succinct: as long as they need to be and not one word longer; prose must be clear enough to describe context, methods, and insights fully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure clear, well-organized sentences and paragraphs; eliminate typographical, spelling, and grammar errors. Reviewers should avoid commenting on authors' linguistic qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure and table accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures avoid use of red/green that may be hard for color blind readers to see.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use color palettes and contrasts accessible to color-blind readers; ensure figure font sizes and line widths are large enough to be legible when reproduced at typical printed sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure clarity and focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures need not show all data broken down in all possible ways: figures should convey a result as simply and directly as possible, focusing readers' attention on key trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use color where appropriate to clearly distinguish lines; avoid overloading figures with unnecessary breakdowns—present essential trends clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary materials must be nonessential
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary Materials enrich the results but are not essential elements to understand the core message of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imagine if the Supplement were lost; the main paper should remain understandable. If material is essential, move it into the main text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics for vertebrate animal research
rubrics_metrics.description: For vertebrate animal research, authors describe animal care approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide institutional approvals and compliance statements for animal care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics for human subjects research
rubrics_metrics.description: For human subjects, authors describe institutional research approval (e.g., IRB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State IRB or equivalent approvals and consent procedures as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population viability consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The research does not pose a threat to population viability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure field or experimental work does not jeopardize populations; justify sampling intensity and provide safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field study permits and location reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors report information about collecting permits (if needed) and list specific locations (e.g., coordinates) where samples were collected or experiments performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide permit details and precise locations; exceptions allowed (e.g., to protect threatened populations). Also report dates of field work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about intent and post-hoc analyses ✪
rubrics_metrics.description: It is good practice to state whether the research was initially planned to address the topic reported or whether the paper reports post-hoc analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be open about relationship between initial intent and final findings; post-hoc studies are acceptable but should be transparently framed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preregistration disclosure (aspirational) ✪
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to state whether the study design or statistical analysis was preregistered; absence of preregistration is not penalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State preregistration status; the journal encourages but does not require preregistration or penalize deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of subjects to treatments (sampling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors report how study subjects were allocated to experimental treatments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe randomization or allocation schemes to allow readers to assess potential biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors state how sample sizes were chosen (e.g., describe a power analysis, or logistical constraints).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rationale for sample sizes, including power analyses when feasible or practical/logistical reasons if not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source identification for genetic stocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors identify sources of genetic stocks, where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report provenance of strains, lines, populations, or cultures used in the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental treatment magnitude and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors state the magnitude of experimental treatments (e.g., food rations, pH levels), and describe how these magnitudes were chosen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quantitative treatment values and biological/experimental justification for chosen levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding of observers
rubrics_metrics.description: Observers recording data were blind to the experimental treatment imposed on the research subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe blinding procedures used to reduce observer bias; if not possible, explain why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voucher specimen deposition
rubrics_metrics.description: If voucher specimens are available, authors identify where they are deposited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide repository information and accession numbers where applicable to enable verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed protocols for nonstandard methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors provide detailed protocols for nonstandard methods as supplementary materials, including reagents, concentrations, plasticware, vendors, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include enough procedural detail to permit exact replication; deposit protocols in Supplementary Materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting sample sizes for all data and subsets
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors report sample sizes for all data, including subsets of data (e.g., each treatment group, other subsets), and sample size used for all statistical analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about N in every analysis and every table/figure; differentiate between biological and technical replicates where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify level of replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors identify the level of replication relevant to a given analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify observational units (e.g., individuals, plots, populations) and the replication structure used in statistical tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise details of data analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors provide the precise details of data analysis (software, packages with citations to authors, and descriptions of each statistical test).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include software versions, package citations, and exact tests used so analyses are reproducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report effect sizes and uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors provide estimates of effect size and uncertainty in these estimates. Tests of statistical significance that omit effect sizes are omitting the biology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present effect sizes (e.g., coefficients, mean differences) with confidence intervals or other uncertainty measures rather than relying solely on p-values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge exploratory analyses and model selection
rubrics_metrics.description: If exploratory analyses were performed, then only a subset of models reported in the paper, authors should acknowledge all exploratory analyses and explain the choice of final focal models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about exploratory vs confirmatory analyses and rationale for choosing final models; describe model selection procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report estimated effects for all model variables
rubrics_metrics.description: In reporting model results, authors should report estimated effects for all model variables (this may be in Supplementary materials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full parameter estimates (with uncertainty) for transparency, even for control variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide analysis code for review and readers ✪
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should make the code to replicate data analysis available for review and for readers after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit code with manuscript or provide a link that does not reveal reviewer identity during review. Code should be self-contained and well-annotated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report measures describing meta-analysis scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors identify the scope of the meta-analysis: range of dates, geography, taxonomy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly delimit the population of studies considered to contextualize results and generality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe search criteria and databases for meta-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors describe the search criteria used to obtain information, including databases and keywords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full search strings, databases searched, and any limits applied to allow reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include antonyms in keyword searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Keyword searches include antonyms to catch negative effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design search strategies to avoid biasing results toward positive findings; explicitly include terms that would capture negative effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion/exclusion criteria for meta-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors describe criteria for including or excluding studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State explicit, pre-specified rules for study selection and how ambiguous cases were handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data extraction and repeatability in meta-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors describe how data was extracted from relevant studies, include software citations where relevant, and state whether duplicate observers obtain replicate data extracts to evaluate repeatability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report extraction protocols, software used, and inter-extractor agreement or procedures to resolve discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-analysis effect size measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors state measures of effect size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define the metric(s) used (e.g., standardized mean difference, odds ratio) and justify choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighting methods or justification in meta-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors state methods for weighting studies by confidence, or justify the lack thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain weighting schemes (e.g., inverse-variance) or rationalize unweighted approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for non-independence and pseudoreplication in meta-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors state how analyses accounted for pseudoreplication arising from multiple effect size estimates within one study population or species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multilevel models, sensitivity analyses, or other approaches to handle non-independence and report the approach taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phylogenetic corrections in meta-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Were phylogenetic corrections applied to adjust for non-independence of study species?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relevant, describe phylogenetic models or justify not using them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain statistical model choices in meta-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors clearly explain statistical model choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rationale for fixed vs random effects, model selection, and assumptions underlying chosen models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report exclusions and reasons after data acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors state whether any data points were excluded after data acquisition, and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document exclusions transparently and assess sensitivity to those exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate publication bias
rubrics_metrics.description: How was publication bias evaluated?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use funnel plots, trim-and-fill, Egger's test, p-curve, or other appropriate diagnostics and report results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report handling of missing data in meta-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors explain how many entries suffer from missing data, and how these missing data were handled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe imputation, exclusion, or modeling approaches for missing moderators or outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide meta-analysis code and data upon submission ✪
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon submission, we encourage authors to provide a copy of the statistical code used to analyze the data, along with necessary data files (see Submission Formatting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include code/data with submission where feasible to facilitate review; ensure reviewer anonymity is preserved when using external repositories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report numbers of studies passing inclusion filters (meta-analysis results)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors state the number of studies that passed various filters for inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide flow diagram or table documenting screening and inclusion steps (e.g., PRISMA-style).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report effect size distribution and uncertainty (meta-analysis results)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors provide measures of both effect size, variance in effect size, and confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present pooled effect estimates, heterogeneity metrics (e.g., I^2), and confidence/credible intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe possible sources of bias in available data (meta-analysis results)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors describe possible sources of bias in the available data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss study-level biases, reporting biases, geographic/taxonomic gaps, and how these may influence conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological motive for theory papers
rubrics_metrics.description: All theory published in The American Naturalist should aim to explain or anticipate a biological phenomenon and must clearly describe the underlying biology with suitable references to empirical results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe specific biological examples and relate model assumptions to empirical cases; compare model output to relevant empirical data when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relate model assumptions to biological examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should relate model assumptions to biological examples, where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify assumptions by citing empirical studies or explaining biological relevance of simplifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain rationale for analytical vs simulation methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should explain the rationale behind choosing analytical versus simulation methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify method choice in terms of tractability, biological realism, and the questions asked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain deterministic vs stochastic and time representation choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should explain the rationale behind choosing a deterministic versus stochastic model and justify the choice of continuous versus discrete time as relevant to the underlying biology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss pros/cons and biological relevance of modeling choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define all symbols and recommend symbol tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must define all symbols where they are first used. Tables of symbols are recommended, and must be in the main text if they describe variables used in the main text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although symbol tables can interrupt flow, include them when they improve clarity; ensure every variable/symbol is defined on first use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base functional choices on empirical trends when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: When possible, the choice of a function for a biological relationship should be based on empirical trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select functional forms informed by data or cite empirical work supporting functional choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: State and justify assumptions and simplifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should clearly state assumptions and simplifications and where possible justify the assumptions with reference to empirical data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly list assumptions and discuss their biological plausibility and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize meaning of equations in prose
rubrics_metrics.description: To reach an empirical audience, the meaning of each equation must be clearly summarized in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe in words what equations imply about biology and the direction/magnitude of effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameter range specification and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: The range of parameters should be clearly stated and, when possible, justified with reference to biological information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide empirical bases or literature citations for parameter ranges used in analysis or simulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explore parameter space sufficiently
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple parameters are involved, parameter space should be explored sufficiently widely to evaluate interactions among key parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sensitivity analyses and explore combinations of parameter values to assess robustness of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derive analytical solutions clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytical solutions should be clearly derived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show derivations or append them in Supplementary Materials to allow verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify approximations and discuss consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximations and simplifications should be clearly identified, and their consequences discussed (e.g., when assuming very weak selection to obtain an analytical result, consider what the consequences are if selection is strong).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss limits of approximations and perform checks where possible (e.g., via simulation) to assess their impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share simulation code with reviewers and publicly
rubrics_metrics.description: Simulation code should be made available to reviewers and subsequently should be shared on a public repository. Note that sharing your Github page can reveal your identity, so submitting a code file as an attachment with your manuscript is preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide runnable code with documentation; during peer review prefer attached code files to avoid revealing author identity via public repo links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript formatting required items
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuous line numbers or page numbers and line numbers are required for peer review. Manuscripts must be double-spaced. Fonts for math should be embedded in the pdf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure submissions include line/page numbers, are double-spaced, and embed math fonts to avoid rendering issues for reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation formatting for initial submission (recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal does not require precise American Naturalist-style citation formatting for initial submission, but this is required for a final accepted version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While initial submissions may relax strict formatting, reviewers may be critical of citation formats that clearly deviate from journal style; prepare to fix citations for final submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript structure guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal does not adhere rigidly to Introduction-Methods-Results-Discussion formatting; Methods should always be described before Results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative structures are acceptable when warranted (e.g., model+data papers), but ensure Methods appear prior to Results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of figures and tables in main text
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage authors to put figures and tables in the main text, where they are first mentioned, with captions on the same page. Preferably, figures should be on the same page as the caption that describes them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many reviewers prefer figures/tables placed where first cited; doing so reduces reviewer friction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code quality and annotation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofread your code as carefully as you proofread your manuscript prose. Code should be carefully annotated to state dependencies and the purpose of each step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotate code, state library dependencies and versions, and explain the purpose of scripts/functions to facilitate reuse and review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-contained code
rubrics_metrics.description: Code should be self-contained so a user with the relevant input data files can recreate your results, without extraneous code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide only the necessary scripts and a clear README describing how to run analyses; avoid including unrelated files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of data tables and analytical code (strong encouragement) ✪
rubrics_metrics.description: We strongly encourage authors, when feasible, to submit data tables and analytical code (e.g., an R markdown file) alongside the manuscript, so editors and reviewers can check the code with the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These may be submitted with the paper, or provided via a link to a GitHub repository or equivalent; files shared through an external website that might reveal reviewer identity are not acceptable for review and may cause the paper to be returned for correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare Dryad data package before submission (aspirational) ✪
rubrics_metrics.description: We encourage authors to have their Dryad data package (data files, metadata, and ReadMe) prepared before submission, and to make these files available for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Having a ready data package expedites data sharing after acceptance and facilitates transparent review when appropriate.
